title: Acids and bases - 123 school
heading: Acids and bases
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What is an acid?
questions.a: A particle that can donate an H<sup>+</sup>

questions.q: What is a base?
questions.a: A particle that can accept an H<sup>+</sup>

questions.q: What pH does an acidic solution have?
What pH does a neutral solution have at 298 K?
What is the [H<sup>+</sup>] in a solution with pH = 3?
Calculate the pH of 0.010 mol/L hydrochloric acid (HCl).
questions.a: 2.00: HCl is a strong acid, so [H<sup>+</sup>] = 0.010 mol/L; pH = −log 0.010 = 2.00

questions.q: Calculate the pH of 0.0010 mol/L nitric acid (HNO<sub>3</sub>).
questions.a: 3.00: HNO<sub>3</sub> is a strong acid, so [H<sup>+</sup>] = 0.0010 mol/L; pH = −log 0.0010 = 3.00

questions.q: Calculate the pH of 0.010 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution (NaOH).
questions.a: 12.00: NaOH is a strong base, so [OH<sup>-</sup>] = 0.010 mol/L; pOH = 2.00 and pH = 14 − 2.00 = 12.00

questions.q: Calculate the pH of 1.0 × 10<sup>-4</sup> mol/L sodium hydroxide solution (NaOH).
Calculate the pH of 0.0050 mol/L barium hydroxide, Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub> (a strong base).
questions.a: 12.00: Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub> → Ba<sup>2+</sup> + 2 OH<sup>-</sup>, so [OH<sup>-</sup>] = 2 × 0.0050 = 0.010 mol/L; pOH = 2.00 and pH = 12.00

questions.q: What is the relationship between pH and pOH at 298 K?
A solution has [H<sup>+</sup>] = 2.5 × 10<sup>-4</sup> mol/L. Calculate the pH.
How many times as great is the [H<sup>+</sup>] at pH = 2 as at pH = 4?
questions.a: 100 times: a difference of 2 pH units is 10<sup>2</sup> = 100

questions.q: A solution of a strong acid has pH = 2.0. You dilute the solution 10 times with water. What is the new pH?
questions.a: 3.0: the [H<sup>+</sup>] becomes 10 times as small, so the pH becomes 1 higher

questions.q: You dilute 10 mL of 1.0 mol/L HCl to 100 mL. What is the new concentration?
What does it mean that HCl is a strong acid?
questions.a: All HCl molecules donate their H<sup>+</sup> to water

questions.q: What does it mean that acetic acid is a weak acid?
questions.a: Only a small fraction of the molecules donates an H<sup>+</sup> (equilibrium)

What is the notation for a solution of the strong acid HNO<sub>3</sub>?
What is the formula of nitric acid?
What is the conjugate acid of NH<sub>3</sub>?
What is the conjugate base of HCO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>?
Which particle can react both as an acid and as a base (ampholyte)? (use BINAS table 49)
What is the reaction equation for the neutralisation of hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide solution (in ions)?
Acetic acid reacts with sodium hydroxide solution. What is the equation of the acid–base reaction?
Ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>) reacts with hydrochloric acid. What is the equation of the acid–base reaction?
You neutralise 25.0 mL of hydrochloric acid with 20.0 mL of 0.100 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution. Calculate the concentration of the hydrochloric acid.
How many mL of 0.200 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution is needed to neutralise 10.0 mL of 0.100 mol/L hydrochloric acid?
How many mL of 0.200 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution is needed to neutralise 20.0 mL of 0.100 mol/L sulfuric acid (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>)?
questions.a: 20.0 mL: n(H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>) = 0.0200 × 0.100 = 2.00 × 10<sup>-3</sup> mol; each H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> gives 2 H<sup>+</sup>, so n(NaOH) = 4.00 × 10<sup>-3</sup> mol; V = 4.00 × 10<sup>-3</sup> : 0.200 = 0.0200 L = 20.0 mL

questions.q: A weak acid HZ has Ka = 1.0 × 10<sup>-5</sup> and a concentration of 0.10 mol/L. Calculate the pH. (Assume that [H<sup>+</sup>] = [Z<sup>-</sup>] and that [HZ] ≈ 0.10 mol/L.)
questions.a: 3.00: Ka = [H<sup>+</sup>]<sup>2</sup> : 0.10, so [H<sup>+</sup>] = square root of (1.0 × 10<sup>-5</sup> × 0.10) = 1.0 × 10<sup>-3</sup> mol/L; pH = 3.00

questions.q: Four acids have these acid constants: HA 1 × 10<sup>-3</sup>, HB 1 × 10<sup>-5</sup>, HC 1 × 10<sup>-8</sup>, HD 1 × 10<sup>-10</sup>. Which acid is the strongest?
questions.a: HA: the greater the Ka, the stronger the acid

questions.q: What colour does litmus have at pH = 2? (use BINAS table 52A)
What colour does phenolphthalein have at pH = 2? (use BINAS table 52A)
Explain why water is an ampholyte.
questions.a: Water can accept an H<sup>+</sup> (H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>) and donate an H<sup>+</sup> (OH<sup>-</sup>), so it reacts as a base and as an acid

questions.q: What happens to the pH if you dilute an acidic solution with water? Explain.
questions.a: The pH becomes higher (towards 7), because the concentration of H<sup>+</sup> becomes smaller
